sections.html: Hyphessobrycon epicharis was first scientifically described in 1997 and is on the dream list of many tetra enthusiasts. The unique feature of this Rosy tetra is the shape of its shoulder spot, which distinguishes it from all other species.

The importers were able to bring in this tetra for the first time. The fish are magnificent and very elegant, even though they hardly show any red colour, contrary to many pictures on the internet. This is obviously a matter of local populations. The exact origin of these animals is unknown; they were exported from Brazil.

The animals are unfortunately very expensive and will certainly be welcomed by tetra specialists. It is assumed that breeding will succeed soon and that they will become accessible to a wider public.

The specimens on which the first description was based came from the upper reaches of the Rio Baria in the Cerro de Neblina area in the extreme south of Venezuela (Territorio Federal Amazonas) on the border with Brazil; no ornamental fish are exported from there. It later turned out that the species is much more widespread in Venezuela and Brazil (upper Rio Negro, Casiquiare and upper Orinoco), but always away from the usual fishing routes.

The first live photo was brought by Hans-Georg Evers in 2000 with a cuvette photo of the Rio Miuá taken at the site. Later Kai Arend was able to photograph a pair in the aquarium of a guide in Venezuela, which he had caught above the mouth of the Rio Ventuari into the Orinoco and brought home.

During the photo session there were three males and one female in the aquarium, and the female dominated the males. The females are the more active part during courtship. During courtship the fish develop a smoky dark coloration due to expansion of the black pigment cells (melanophores), while otherwise they are crystal-transparent with a red tinge.
The females differ clearly from the males by the coloration of the dorsal fin.
